This file is a merged representation of the entire codebase, combined into a single document by Repomix.
The content has been processed where line numbers have been added.

# File Summary

## Purpose
This file contains a packed representation of the entire repository's contents.
It is designed to be easily consumable by AI systems for analysis, code review,
or other automated processes.

## File Format
The content is organized as follows:
1. This summary section
2. Repository information
3. Directory structure
4. Repository files (if enabled)
5. Multiple file entries, each consisting of:
  a. A header with the file path (## File: path/to/file)
  b. The full contents of the file in a code block

## Usage Guidelines
- This file should be treated as read-only. Any changes should be made to the
  original repository files, not this packed version.
- When processing this file, use the file path to distinguish
  between different files in the repository.
- Be aware that this file may contain sensitive information. Handle it with
  the same level of security as you would the original repository.

## Notes
- Some files may have been excluded based on .gitignore rules and Repomix's configuration
- Binary files are not included in this packed representation. Please refer to the Repository Structure section for a complete list of file paths, including binary files
- Files matching patterns in .gitignore are excluded
- Files matching default ignore patterns are excluded
- Line numbers have been added to the beginning of each line
- Files are sorted by Git change count (files with more changes are at the bottom)

 1: name: CD
 2: 
 3: on:
 4:   push:

 6: 
 7: permissions:

10: 
11: jobs:
12:   publish:
13:     name: Publish Docker image
14:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
15:     steps:
16:       - name: Check out repository
17:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
18:       - name: Read application version
19:         id: version
20:         shell: bash
21:         run: echo "version=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
22:       - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
23:         uses: docker/login-action@v3
24:         with:
25:           registry: ghcr.io
26:           username: ${{ github.actor }}
27:           password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
28:       - name: Generate image metadata
29:         id: meta
30:         uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
31:         with:
32:           images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
33:           tags: |
34:             type=sha
35:             type=raw,value=v${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
36:             type=raw,value=latest
37:       - name: Set up Docker Buildx
38:         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
39:       - name: Build and publish production image
40:         uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
41:         with:
42:           context: .
43:           push: true
44:           tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
45:           labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
46:           cache-from: type=gha
47:           cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
````

52:

63:         with:
64:           context: .
65:           push: false
66:           tags: thread-match:${{ github.sha }}
67:           cache-from: type=gha
68:           cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

12: .close{width:40px;height:40px;padding:0;display:grid;place-items:center;line-height:1;z-index:1}.x-symbol{position:relative;display:block;width:18px;height:18px}.x-symbol::before,.x-symbol::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:8px;top:-1px;width:3px;height:20px;border-radius:2px;background:currentColor}.x-symbol::before{transform:rotate(45deg)}.x-symbol::after{transform:rotate(-45deg)}.detail-actions button{display:grid;place-items:center;padding:0}.detail-actions .x-symbol{width:16px;height:16px}.detail-actions .x-symbol::before,.detail-actions .x-symbol::after{left:7px;width:2px;height:18px}.discover .actions .x-symbol{width:20px;height:20px}.discover .actions .x-symbol::before,.discover .actions .x-symbol::after{left:9px;width:3px;height:22px}
13: .discover .actions .dislike span.x-symbol{transform:none}
14: .detail-summary{touch-action:pan-y;cursor:grab;transition:transform .2s ease}.detail-summary.is-dragging{cursor:grabbing;transition:none}.detail-summary.is-exiting,.discover-swipe.is-exiting{transition:transform .22s ease-in}
15: .discover{overflow-x:hidden}.discover-swipe{touch-action:pan-y;cursor:grab;transition:transform .2s ease}.discover-swipe.is-dragging{cursor:grabbing;transition:none}.overlay{overflow-x:hidden}
16: .discover{overflow-x:visible}body{overflow-x:hidden}

18: .outfit-selects{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:.7rem}.outfit-selects select{width:100%;margin:0}.canvas{width:max-content;max-width:100%;margin:1rem auto 0;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#17191f,#252a33);border:1px solid #3a414d;min-height:0;padding:1rem;border-radius:20px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:stretch;justify-content:center;gap:.7rem;font-size:1rem}.outfit-piece{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:.9rem;padding:.6rem .8rem;border:1px solid #3a414d;border-radius:12px;background:#20252d;color:#f5f7fb;box-shadow:0 6px 14px #0004}.outfit-piece img{width:56px;height:56px;flex:none;object-fit:contain;border-radius:8px;background:#f5f7fb}.outfit-piece span{color:#f5f7fb;font-weight:600;line-height:1.25}.narrow select{background:#17191f;color:#f5f7fb;border:1px solid #3a414d}.narrow select:focus{outline:2px solid #ff4f86;outline-offset:2px}
19: @media(max-width:600px){.detail-summary{gap:.8rem}.detail-summary>img{width:88px;height:88px}.detail-summary h2{font-size:1.2rem}.similar{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr}.similar .card img{width:56px;height:56px}}
20: @media(max-width:600px){.outfit-selects{grid-template-columns:1fr}.canvas{width:100%}}
21: :root{color:#f5f7fb;background:#080a0e}body{min-height:100vh;background:radial-gradient(circle at 50% -20%,#20242d 0%,#0d1015 38%,#080a0e 100%)}header{background:#0d1015;border-bottom-color:#252a33}header nav button{color:#8f98a8}.active{color:#fff!important;border-bottom-color:#ff4f86}.content>h2,.content h2{color:#f5f7fb}
22: header .link{align-self:center;margin-top:0;color:#8f98a8;padding:.5rem}header .link:hover{color:#fff}header nav button,header .link{transition:color .15s,transform .15s}header nav button:active,header .link:active{transform:translateY(1px)}
23: .actions button,.detail-actions button{transition:transform .15s ease,box-shadow .15s ease,filter .15s ease}.actions button:hover,.detail-actions button:hover{transform:scale(1.08);filter:brightness(1.08);box-shadow:0 8px 18px #0006}.actions button:active,.detail-actions button:active{transform:scale(.92);box-shadow:0 2px 6px #0006}.actions button:focus-visible,.detail-actions button:focus-visible,header .link:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #ff4f86;outline-offset:3px}
24: .auth{background:radial-gradient(circle at 50% -20%,#20242d 0%,#0d1015 38%,#080a0e 100%);color:#f5f7fb}.panel{background:#111419;border:1px solid #30343d;box-shadow:0 20px 50px #0009}.panel h1,.panel h2{color:#f5f7fb}.panel .muted{color:#aeb5c2}.panel input{background:#17191f;color:#f5f7fb;border-color:#3a414d}.panel input::placeholder{color:#8f98a8}.panel input:focus{outline:2px solid #ff4f86;outline-offset:1px}.panel>button:not(.link){background:#ff4f86;color:#fff}.panel>button:not(.link):hover{background:#ff6a9b}.panel .link{color:#aeb5c2}.panel .link:hover{color:#fff}.panel small{color:#8f98a8}
````

## File: scripts/check-version.mjs
````javascript
 1: import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
 2: import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
 3: 
 4: const baseRef = process.argv[2];
 5: if (!baseRef) {
 6:   console.error('Usage: npm run check:version -- <base-commit>');
 7:   process.exit(1);
 8: }
 9: 
10: const readVersion = (contents, source, required = true) => {
11:   let packageJson;
12:   try {
13:     packageJson = JSON.parse(contents);
14:   } catch {
15:     throw new Error(`Could not parse ${source}`);
16:   }
17: 
18:   if (typeof packageJson.version !== 'string') {
19:     if (!required) return null;
20:     throw new Error(`${source} does not define a version`);
21:   }
22: 
23:   const match = packageJson.version.match(/^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:-([0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?$/);
24:   if (!match) {
25:     throw new Error(`${source} has invalid semver: ${packageJson.version}`);
26:   }
27: 
28:   return {
29:     text: packageJson.version,
30:     major: Number(match[1]),
31:     minor: Number(match[2]),
32:     patch: Number(match[3]),
33:     prerelease: match[4] ?? ''
34:   };
35: };
36: 
37: const compareVersions = (left, right) => {
38:   for (const key of ['major', 'minor', 'patch']) {
39:     if (left[key] !== right[key]) return left[key] - right[key];
40:   }
41: 
42:   if (!left.prerelease && right.prerelease) return 1;
43:   if (left.prerelease && !right.prerelease) return -1;
44:   return left.prerelease.localeCompare(right.prerelease);
45: };
46: 
47: let baseContents;
48: try {
49:   baseContents = execFileSync('git', ['show', `${baseRef}:package.json`], {encoding: 'utf8'});
50: } catch {
51:   console.error(`Could not read package.json from base commit ${baseRef}`);
52:   process.exit(1);
53: }
54: 
55: try {
56:   const baseVersion = readVersion(baseContents, 'base package.json', false);
57:   const currentVersion = readVersion(readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8'), 'current package.json');
58: 
59:   if (!baseVersion) {
60:     console.log(`Version check passed: initial version ${currentVersion.text}`);
61:     process.exit(0);
62:   }
63: 
64:   if (compareVersions(currentVersion, baseVersion) <= 0) {
65:     throw new Error(`Version must increase from ${baseVersion.text} to a newer version (current: ${currentVersion.text})`);
66:   }
67: 
68:   console.log(`Version check passed: ${baseVersion.text} -> ${currentVersion.text}`);
69: } catch (error) {
70:   console.error(error.message);
71:   process.exit(1);
72: }
````

## File: server/db/001_schema.sql
````sql
 1: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;
 2: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
 3:  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
 4:  first_name TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
 5: );
 6: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_preferences (
 7:  user_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 8:  preferred_colors TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', preferred_shirt_styles TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
 9:  preferred_pant_styles TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', preferred_materials TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
10:  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
11: );
12: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clothing_items (
13:  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL,
14:  subcategory TEXT NOT NULL, gender_tag TEXT NOT NULL, color TEXT NOT NULL, style TEXT NOT NULL,
15:  material TEXT NOT NULL, image_url TEXT NOT NULL, price NUMERIC(10,2),
16:  source_id INTEGER UNIQUE, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
17: );
18: ALTER TABLE clothing_items ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id INTEGER;
19: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS clothing_items_source_id_idx ON clothing_items(source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL;
20: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_interactions (
21:  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
22:  item_id UUID REFERENCES clothing_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, interaction_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (interaction_type IN ('like','dislike')),
23:  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE(user_id,item_id)
24: );
25: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS interactions_user_idx ON user_interactions(user_id);
26: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS items_category_idx ON clothing_items(category,subcategory);

4:   if (!token) return res.status(401).json({error:'Authentication required'});
5:   try { req.user = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'dev-secret'); next(); }

## File: server/src/catalogImport.js
````javascript
  1: import fs from 'node:fs';
  2: import path from 'node:path';

 12: const csvFields = (line) => {
 13:   const fields = [];

 15:   let quoted = false;

 17:     if (character === '"') quoted = !quoted;
 18:     else if (character === ',' && !quoted) {
 19:       fields.push(field);
 20:       field = '';
 21:     } else field += character;

 23:   fields.push(field);
 24:   return fields.map(value => value.replace(/^"|"$/g, '').replace(/""/g, '"'));
 25: };
 26: 
 27: const categoryFor = (subCategory, masterCategory) => {
 28:   if (subCategory === 'Topwear') return 'tops';
 29:   if (subCategory === 'Bottomwear') return 'bottoms';
 30:   if (subCategory === 'Socks') return 'socks';
 31:   if (subCategory === 'Belts') return 'belts';
 32:   if (subCategory === 'Eyewear') return 'sunglasses';
 33:   if (['Shoes', 'Sandal', 'Flip Flops'].includes(subCategory)) return 'shoes';
 34:   if (masterCategory === 'Apparel') return 'tops';
 35:   return 'accessories';
 36: };
 37: 
 38: const toItem = (values) => {
 39:   const [id, gender, masterCategory, subCategory, articleType, baseColour, season, year, usage, productDisplayName] = values;
 40:   return {
 41:     sourceId: Number(id),
 42:     name: productDisplayName,
 43:     category: categoryFor(subCategory, masterCategory),
 44:     subcategory: articleType.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, '-'),
 45:     genderTag: gender.toLowerCase(),
 46:     color: baseColour.toLowerCase(),
 47:     style: usage.toLowerCase(),
 48:     material: masterCategory.toLowerCase(),
 49:     imageUrl: `/catalog-images/${id}.jpg`,
 50:     price: null
 51:   };
 52: };
 53: 
 54: async function insertBatch(items) {
 55:   if (!items.length) return;
 56:   const values = [];
 57:   const params = [];
 58:   for (const item of items) {
 59:     const offset = params.length;
 60:     values.push(`($${offset + 1},$${offset + 2},$${offset + 3},$${offset + 4},$${offset + 5},$${offset + 6},$${offset + 7},$${offset + 8},$${offset + 9},$${offset + 10})`);
 61:     params.push(item.name, item.category, item.subcategory, item.genderTag, item.color, item.style, item.material, item.imageUrl, item.price, item.sourceId);
 62:   }
 63:   await query(`INSERT INTO clothing_items (name,category,subcategory,gender_tag,color,style,material,image_url,price,source_id)
 64:     VALUES ${values.join(',')} ON CONFLICT (source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING`, params);
 65: }

 69:     console.warn(`Kaggle catalog not found at ${csvPath}; no catalog rows imported.`);
 70:     return;
 71:   }
 72:   await query('ALTER TABLE clothing_items ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id INTEGER');
 73:   await query('ALTER TABLE clothing_items ALTER COLUMN price DROP NOT NULL');
 74:   await query('CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS clothing_items_source_id_idx ON clothing_items(source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL');
 75:   await query(`UPDATE clothing_items SET category='socks' WHERE subcategory='socks'`);
 76:   await query(`UPDATE clothing_items SET category='belts' WHERE subcategory='belts'`);
 77:   await query(`UPDATE clothing_items SET category='sunglasses' WHERE subcategory='eyewear'`);
 78:   const existing = await query('SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM clothing_items WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL');
 79:   if (existing.rows[0].count >= 40000) return;

 81:   await query('DELETE FROM user_interactions');
 82:   await query('DELETE FROM clothing_items WHERE source_id IS NULL');
 83:   await query('DELETE FROM clothing_items WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL');

 85:   const input = readline.createInterface({input: fs.createReadStream(csvPath), crlfDelay: Infinity});

 87:   let items = [];

 90:       header = false;
 91:       continue;
 92:     }
 93:     if (!line.trim()) continue;
 94:     const values = csvFields(line);
 95:     if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dataRoot, 'images', `${values[0]}.jpg`))) items.push(toItem(values));
 96:     if (items.length === batchSize) {

## File: server/src/recommendationEngine.js
````javascript
1: const fields = ['color','style','material'];
2: const arr = (v) => Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(String).map(x => x.toLowerCase()) : [];
3: export function scoreItem(item, preferences = {}, signals = {likes: [], dislikes: []}) {
4:   const explicit = fields.reduce((n, field) => n + (arr(preferences[`preferred_${field === 'style' ? 'shirt_styles' : field + 's'}`]).includes(String(item[field]).toLowerCase()) ? 1 : 0), 0) / 3;
5:   const likes = signals.likes || [], dislikes = signals.dislikes || [];
6:   const learned = fields.reduce((n, field) => n + (likes.filter(x => x[field] === item[field]).length ? 1 : 0), 0) / 3;
7:   const penalty = fields.filter(field => dislikes.filter(x => x[field] === item[field]).length).length / 3;
8:   return Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Math.round((explicit * 0.65 + learned * 0.35) * 100 * (1 - penalty * 0.65))));
9: }
````

16:     expect(schema).toMatch(/REFERENCES users\(id\) ON DELETE CASCADE/i);
17:     expect(schema).toMatch(/REFERENCES clothing_items\(id\) ON DELETE CASCADE/i);
18:   });
19: 
20:   test('enforces valid interaction types and unique user-item interactions', () => {
21:     expect(schema).toMatch(/CHECK \(interaction_type IN \('like','dislike'\)\)/i);
22:     expect(schema).toMatch(/UNIQUE\(user_id,item_id\)/i);
23:     expect(schema).toMatch(/CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS items_category_idx/i);
24:   });
25: });
````

  1: # Thread Match
  2: 
  3: Thread Match is a runnable clothing recommendation MVP. It combines onboarding preferences with explicit like/dislike history, returning a transparent 0-100 match score.

 17: - [Docker](#docker)

 20: - [CI/CD](#cicd)
 21:

 23: 
 24: ```text

 26: ├── .github/
 27: │   └── workflows/       # GitHub Actions CI and CD workflows
 28: ├── client/
 29: │   ├── src/

 53: ## App pages
 54: 
 55: The application uses a shared top navigation bar after authentication. The sections below describe each page and include a placeholder where screenshots can be added later.
 56: 
 57: ### Sign in and registration
 58: 
 59: The entry page lets returning users sign in with their email and password. New users can create an account by providing their first name, email, and password. The page displays validation and authentication errors without leaving the current view, and provides a link for switching between the two modes.
 60: 
 61: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cc1d377-d7a5-4c30-8282-eae3c731144d" />
 62: 
 63: ### Onboarding
 64: 
 65: After creating an account, the onboarding flow asks users to select preferences across four categories: colors, shirt styles, pant styles, and materials. Each step uses selectable chips, shows progress through the four-step flow, and requires at least one selection before continuing. The final step saves the preferences and opens the main application.
 66: 
 67: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fac40d1-3742-4362-8b1a-c8e054b13df0" />
 68: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78814885-cd0a-4e8a-8e92-ac69094b0ff1" />
 69: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68fbf575-36a0-48cd-8245-6cce5fe8f524" />
 70: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0b471d5-052f-4dc2-a1d9-a78b5ca5f8f0" />
 71: 
 72: 
 73: ### Discover
 74: 
 75: The Discover page presents a daily clothing recommendation in the “Daily Edit.” Users can inspect the item, like it, or dislike it. The card supports mouse and touch dragging: swiping right likes the item and swiping left dislikes it. After an action, the current card exits the screen and the next item loads in the same position. A loading placeholder is shown while the next item is being retrieved.
 76: 
 77: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b23be77c-6bbb-406d-b45b-499c7843bf74" />
 78: 
 79: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9efb96ce-5f6e-478b-9647-7e06e4738375" />
 80: 
 81: 
 82: ### Suggested
 83: 
 84: The Suggested page displays a grid of recommended clothing items based on the user’s preferences and interaction history. The category filter can narrow the results to all items, tops, bottoms, shoes, socks, belts, or accessories. Selecting an item opens its expanded view, where users can review details, like or dislike the item, swipe through the expanded card, and view similar recommendations.
 85: 
 86: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac4d5b49-bdb7-4b42-bca8-d964f8c617f1" />
 87: 
 88: 
 89: ### Outfits
 90: 
 91: The Outfits page, also called Outfit Studio, lets users assemble an outfit from available clothing categories. Selectors are arranged in a responsive grid, and selected pieces are displayed together on a compact outfit canvas. This page helps users compare individual recommendations as a coordinated look.
 92: 
 93: <img width="1920" height="1200" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84680ed7-11a2-4f1e-84a8-1e02ccec8d91" />
 94: 
 95: 
 96: ### FAQ
 97: 
 98: The FAQ page contains expandable question-and-answer panels with information about the recommendation experience and how the application works. Each question can be opened independently so users can scan the topics without leaving the page.

103: ## Run locally
104: 
105: 1. Install Node.js 20+ and PostgreSQL, or start PostgreSQL with `docker compose up db`.
106: 2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set a long random `JWT_SECRET`.
107: 3. Run `npm install` from the repository root. The workspace installs both the API and Vite app.
108: 4. Start both applications with `npm run dev`. The API is at `http://localhost:3000`; Vite is normally at `http://localhost:5173`.
109: 
110: ## Kaggle catalog data
111: 
112: Download and unzip the Kaggle clothing dataset before starting Docker. From the repository root, create a folder named `kaggledata` and place the dataset files in this layout:
113: 
114: ```text
115: kaggledata/
116: ├── styles.csv
117: └── images/
118:     ├── 10000.jpg
119:     ├── 10001.jpg
120:     └── ...
121: ```
122: 
123: On Windows, right-click the downloaded ZIP file, choose **Extract All**, select the project folder (`clothing-recommendation-system`), and extract it. If the ZIP creates an extra nested folder, move `styles.csv` and the `images` folder directly into:
124: 
125: ```text
126: C:\Users\<your-name>\Documents\code\clothing-recommendation-system\kaggledata
127: ```
128: 
129: You can also extract it from PowerShell:
130: 
131: ```powershell
132: Expand-Archive -Path "$HOME\Downloads\archive.zip" -DestinationPath ".\kaggledata"
133: ```
134: 
135: Verify that these paths exist before starting the app:
136: 
137: ```powershell
138: Test-Path .\kaggledata\styles.csv
139: Test-Path .\kaggledata\images
140: ```
141: 
142: Both commands should return `True`. Docker mounts this folder read-only, imports the catalog when the API starts, and serves the local product images.
143: 
144: The SQL files in `server/db` are mounted into the Postgres container and create the schema on a fresh volume. On startup, the API imports the Myntra catalog from `kaggledata/styles.csv` and serves its matching images from `kaggledata/images`. To reset catalog data, run `docker compose down -v` and start it again.
145: 
146: ## Docker
147: 
148: `docker compose up --build` runs Postgres and a production Node container serving the built React application and API at `http://localhost:3000`. Configure `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, and `PORT` through Compose or an environment file; never commit secrets.
149: 
150: ## API
151: 
152: - `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`
153: - `GET/POST /api/user/preferences` (protected)
154: - `GET /api/discover/next`, `POST /api/discover/swipe` (protected)
155: - `GET /api/recommendations?page=1&limit=12&category=tops`
156: - `GET /api/items/:id`, `GET /api/items/:id/similar`, `GET /api/faq`
157: 
158: All SQL uses parameterized queries. Inputs are bounded/validated, passwords use bcrypt, and protected endpoints require short-lived JWT authentication.
159: 
160: ## Tests
161: 
162: Run the server and database-related tests from the repository root:
163: 
164: ```powershell
165: npm test
166: ```
167: 
168: This runs the Jest suite in `server`, including:
169: 
170: - Recommendation scoring behavior
171: - Database-backed API contracts with mocked database queries
172: - Registration validation and authenticated preference persistence
173: - Database schema tables, relationships, constraints, and indexes
174: 
175: Run the webpage tests separately:
176: 
177: ```powershell
178: npm test --workspace client
179: ```
180: 
181: The client suite uses Vitest, jsdom, and Testing Library to verify the Suggested page expanded-item flow, including opening an item, keeping the close button above the transformed summary, and closing the expanded view.
182: 
183: Run both test suites and the production client build with:
184: 
185: ```powershell
186: npm test
187: npm test --workspace client
188: npm run build
189: ```
190: 
191: The current test suite contains six server tests and one client test. Server database tests do not require a live PostgreSQL instance; schema assertions read `server/db/001_schema.sql`, and API tests mock the database query layer.
192: 
193: ## CI/CD
194: 
195: GitHub Actions run on pull requests and pushes to `dev` and `main`. CI installs dependencies, runs the tests, builds the client, uploads the client build, and builds the production Docker image.
196: 
197: Pull requests targeting `dev` or `main` must increase the root `package.json` version. Use a semantic version such as `1.0.1`, `1.1.0`, or `2.0.0`; the version check compares it with the target branch and fails when it is unchanged or lower. The same check runs on pushes to either branch, so direct pushes and merges cannot leave the branch at the previous version. Configure the `Version bump` check as a required status check in branch protection for both protected branches.
198: 
199: After a merge to `main`, CD publishes the production image to GitHub Container Registry as `latest`, the commit SHA, and the application version:
200: 
201: ```text
202: ghcr.io/<owner>/<repository>:latest
203: ghcr.io/<owner>/<repository>:v<version>
204: ```
````
